headline: Master Trust unit to raise Rs 75 crore via non-convertible debentures

modes.bear: Debt issuance increases the interest burden and financial liabilities on the subsidiary, which could impact consolidated margins.
modes.bull: Raising Rs 75 crore via NCDs provides Master Capital Services with fresh capital to scale its operations and lending activities.
modes.simple: Master Trust's main subsidiary is borrowing Rs 75 crore by issuing debentures to grow its business operations.

summary: Master Trust Limited announced that its wholly-owned subsidiary, Master Capital Services Limited, will raise Rs 75 crore by issuing 75,000 non-convertible debentures (NCDs) at Rs 10,000 per debenture. The press release was submitted to the exchange on November 14, 2026. This fundraising aims to boost the financial resources of the subsidiary company. Retail investors tracking Master Trust can note the capital expansion of its core operating unit.
why_it_matters: Subsidiary raises debt capital for operational expansion.

headline: Master Trust unit to raise Rs 75 crore via NCDs

modes.bear: Issuing debt increases financial liabilities and interest servicing costs for the subsidiary, adding potential risk to the balance sheet.
modes.bull: Raising capital via NCDs provides the subsidiary with dedicated funds to scale operations and capture new financial market opportunities.
modes.simple: Master Trust's subsidiary is raising Rs 75 crore by issuing debentures, which are fixed-income debt instruments used to fund business activities.

summary: Master Trust Limited announced that its wholly-owned subsidiary, Master Capital Services Limited, will raise Rs 75 crore by issuing 75,000 non-convertible debentures (NCDs) at an issue price of Rs 10,000 each. The funds will be secured through the allotment of NCDs to support the subsidiary's business operations. Master Capital Services operates within the group's financial services portfolio. Retail investors can track how this debt deployment impacts the subsidiary's future revenue growth and leverage levels.
why_it_matters: Subsidiary debt expansion affects group leverage and growth capacity.

headline: Master Trust subsidiary starts F&O clearing and settlement services
hook: New revenue stream for Master Trust subsidiary
summary: Master Trust Limited announced that its wholly owned subsidiary, Master Capital Services Limited, has commenced clearing and settlement services for Futures and Options trades on both the NSE and BSE. The services became operational through the Custodian Participant Code starting October 15, 2026. This operational expansion allows the subsidiary to handle settlement workflows directly for derivatives clients on the major domestic exchanges. Retail investors tracking the brokerage and financial services sector can note this structural addition to Master Trust's operational capabilities.
why_it_matters: Brokering arm expands institutional and derivatives processing capabilities.
